newsitem.title: USA: U.S. sweet crudes sold off in softer Gulf market.
newsitem.headline: U.S. sweet crudes sold off in softer Gulf market.

text.p: U.S. cash crude grades saw values cheapen Wednesday, as buyers were scarce for sweet barrels and sour differentials extended a recent bearish turn on sentiment foreign supplies were more than abundant.
Grade players said Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James sold as low as 3 cents and 5 cents over August West Texas Intermediate/Cushing, down 20 cents from earlier this week.
"The only buyers for the LLS were simply putting it into storage," said a cash player.
September LLS was quoted at a 22-25 cents premium to WTI. Second month barrels take center stage after Friday August pipeline scheduling day.
Other August barometers had West Texas Sour/Midland moving lower to deals around $1.50 under WTI, though deals were done as weak as $1.55 and down earlier in the session.

September WTS/Midland talked around $1.70 under level. Traders said the intermediate and long-term sour market looks weak, with Iraqi oil sales expected to resume sometime in August and other foreigns, like Canadian crudes, also flooding into the Gulf.
There were no exciting developments from the United Nations concerning Iraq on Wednesday.

Western diplomats and U.N. officials continue to say the aid distribution plan submitted by Baghdad on Monday will be reviewed and approved by the end of July. Oil sales could then start once Iraq submits a pricing mechanism to control terms of new sales contracts.

Still, market players are uncertain on the details of the "oil-for-food" accord's implementation. Terms of the resolution demand that Iraq sell $1 billion of the $2 billion allotment of crude in two separate 90-day periods. The first 90-day period expires on September 5, leaving markets wondering if and how Iraq would lift and sell so much oil in that small window.

Other numbers floated around late on Tuesday saw August WTI/Cushing Postings sell at $1.75, and September at $1.95. The August/September WTI roll stood at -27 cents, steady from Tuesday. Outright August WTI gained slightly and ended around $19.30-40 a barrel, with September WTI at $19.60-70 a barrel.
Cash dealers said aftermarket trades lifted September WTI to $19.64 a barrel, a penny stronger than NYMEX settlement.
